newsitem.title: UK: British Energy abandons gas plans - report.
newsitem.headline: British Energy abandons gas plans - report.

text.p: British Energy Plc, the privatized nuclear power generator, has decided to abandon plans to diversify into gas generation at Heysham, north west England, the Observer newspaper reported.
No one at British Energy was immediately available for comment.

The newspaper also said that a British Energy spokesman had dismissed as speculation the possibility of its closing one of its headquarters, at Gloucester in southwest England, where over 1,500 people work.
British Energy confirmed in July that it was looking into the possibility of building a gas-powered generating plant next to one of its existing nuclear stations at Heysham, north west England.

The Observer said British Energy would make an announcement on a package of economies in mid-October. British Energy was sold off and floated on the London Stock Exchange in July with partly paid shares priced at 105 pence to institutional investors and at a five pence discount for the retail offer.
